title: I Forwarded the Language-Exchange Signup After They Sold My Seat

parts.text: I arrived at 6:29 p.m. with a paid Meetup seat and a stranger was in it with a Venmo note. The signup the organizer posted said: TRANSFERS ONLY THROUGH THE EVENT PAGE. NO DOOR SALES. I was twenty-six, Spanish B1, holding the QR. Organizer Sol said, "We filled a no-show." I was not a no-show; I was two minutes early. I photographed the Venmo, the signup, and my QR. Then I forwarded the event page rule to the Meetup organizer account Sol used. At 6:33 Meetup support posted why Sol's name was on a door-sale ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Meetup support can see a Venmo door sale against the page rule Sol posted.

social.video_title: They Venmo-sold my language-exchange seat — Part 1/2
social.description: QR in hand, a stranger in my chair, and a no-door-sales rule. I forwarded the page. Would you have stood in the back?

parts.text: Sol called it hustle until support refunded the stranger and restored me. I printed the ticket, the rule, and the photo. I sat. Sol told the circle the page was always about optics. Optics is a word organizers use when Venmo is in a still. Signup policy now has a second line: TWO MINUTES EARLY IS NOT A NO-SHOW. I practice pretérito. Sol uses the page. The chairs finally match the QR.

social.video_title: Two minutes early is not a no-show — Part 2/2
social.description: Door-sale ticket, a restored seat, and a second line on the page. Was hustle ever my QR?
